title: Wave 1 release v002: evaluate every flag a release owns, and stamp the deployed version
notes: A forward-only correction. The v001 source referenced every declared flag literally, so GitHub code-reference evidence was already correct, but its runtime evaluated only the first flag. A service like demo-catalog owning four flags would have produced evaluation evidence for one of them.

v002 evaluates every flag the release owns through a single SDK client, and embeds the release so LaunchDarkly application metadata reports the deployed version. The bounded Production rate probe deliberately stays single-flag so its evaluations-per-hour figure keeps its meaning.

Applied as a new step rather than by rewriting s001: history is append-only and tags are immutable, so v001 remains a real earlier deployable version. That is itself useful evidence for the talk's point that old deployed tags can still evaluate a key the current default branch no longer contains.
